London, 28<sup>th</sup> April 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**General Motors** has proposed handing a controlling stake of more than 50% to the US government.  The nationalisation, in effect, of the biggest US motor manufacturer would be part of a huge debt-for-equity swap as GM tries to shed $44bn (£30bn) of $62bn in crippling liabilities.  But the plan was condemned as “neither reasonable nor adequate”, by bondholders who would get only 10% of the company, forcing them to write off billions of dollars. Existing shareholders would be left with only 1%. GM has offered a 10% stake to bondholders, who are owed $27bn – a tough proposition to swallow. For each $1,000 of loan notes, bondholders would get 225 shares, worth little more than $550 at today’s market price.  GM delivered a blunt warning that unless its creditors accepted the plan, it would declare bankruptcy and leave the courts to carve up the company. GM has deepened cuts that will include 23,000 job losses by 2011, the closure of 16 of its 47 factories in the US and a 42% drop in the number of GM dealers. 

GM will shut its 83-year-old Pontiac marque to focus on just four names in the US: Chevrolet, Cadillac, Buick and GMC. Hummer and Sweden’s Saab will either be sold or closed by next year; Britain’s Vauxhall brand is not under threat.  Under the plan, the US treasury and the United Auto Workers’ union would get 89% of the company between them. In return, the government would write off half of the emergency lending extended to GM.  The union’s shares would replace the billions of dollars due for a trust fund for employees’ healthcare.  The Obama administration insisted that private-sector creditors should get no more than this slim return. But in order to proceed, the proposal must be accepted by 90% of bondholders by a deadline of 1 June.  Rebecca Lindland, analyst at IHS Global Insight, said many bondholders were likely to believe they could get a better deal under a bankruptcy arrangement.  For GM, the challenge is to shrink to a scale where it can break even with sales of 10m cars in the US annually, rather than the previous rate of 15m to 17m. _Source:  The Guardian_ 

**Eurasia Mining** announced progress at its exploration projects in central and north-west Russia. The company drilled two sub-areas at Mochetundra and found that ten holes (of 23) intersected mineralisation.  Two mineralised zones which could develop into an open pittable resource have been defined and the focus is on producing resource estimates for them in 2009.  Meanwhile, new low-grade pgms at its Volchetundra site - the only successful hole of the 28 it dug - suggests the existence of a new zone.  Drilling in the Urals at West Kytlim, a JV with Anglo Platinum, is continuing on several new areas which could house alluvial platinum.  However, it will not be able to announce fast-track production plans until recent changes in mining laws are incorporated and clarified. _Source:  Eurasia Mining_

**Aquarius Platinum** has received an irrevocable undertaking by another shareholder of its takeover target Ridge Mining to vote in favour of the proposed acquisition.  The Gold Mountains International Mining Company, a subsidiary of the Zijin Mining Group and which held 18,4-million shares in Ridge, would vote in favour of the acquisition.  The miner has now received irrevocable undertakings in respect of about 30-million Ridge shares, or 32,7% of its shareholding, to vote in favour of the proposed transaction. Source:  Mining Weekly 

**African Rainbow Minerals and Vale** are planning investments in Zimbabwe worth US$300 million “as soon as a consensus with the Ministry (of Mines) is reached”, said ARM business development director. _Source:  Mining Mx_ 

**Central African Mining and Exploration Company** said that progress to date at its Todal JV Bokai platinum project in Zimbabwe has been exceptional and “…mark the first critical milestone in establishing an operational mine in Zimbabwe to ultimately produce c.120 koz 4E/yr,” said CAMEC CEO Andrew Groves. _Source:  Reuters_
